South Korea blend genuine European pedigree with the emotional weight of a farewell tour. Son Heung-min, one of Asia’s greatest-ever players, has openly suggested this could be his final World Cup, adding a “last dance” narrative to every match. Behind him, Lee Kang-in was part of PSG’s Champions League final run, while Kim Min-jae helped Bayern Munich reach the semi-finals., giving Korea two players operating at the very top of European football.Then there is the symbolism of Hong Myung-bo, hero of 2002, attempting to recapture some of that magic from the touchline. Few teams arrive with such a compelling mix of star power, history and sentiment.
[...]
South Korea are arguably the second-strongest team in Group A behind hosts Mexico, and reaching the knockout rounds is the clear primary goal. Statistical projections have given them roughly a coin-flip-to-better chance of advancing from the group. With the expanded format and a squad boasting elite European talent, qualification for the Round of 32 is the expectation, with the Round of 16 a realistic ambition. Anything beyond that would echo the spirit of 2002.

results.title: Uruguay at the World Cup 2026: Bielsa's Outsiders in Group H · Cup26 AI
highlights:
Uruguay at the World Cup 2026: Bielsa's Outsiders in Group H · Cup26 AI
[...]
Uruguay arrive at the 2026 World Cup carrying enormous history and modest expectations. The two-time champions of 1930 and 1950 qualified the hard way, finishing fourth in CONMEBOL qualifying) with 28 points from 18 matches. Coach Marcelo Bielsa, the 70-year-old Argentine who took charge in May 2023, secured the place but enters the tournament under scrutiny: La Celeste won only three of their final twelve qualifiers and were thrashed 5-1 by the United States in a November friendly, a result Bielsa called shameful. He has confirmed his tenure ends after the World Cup.
[...]
The form questions are real. After leading Uruguay to a third-place finish at Copa América 2024 and famous wins over Brazil and Argentina, Bielsa's intensity has reportedly worn on the squad. Retired captain Luis Suárez publicly criticised the coach's methods, and Bielsa himself admitted his authority had been affected. Whether the dressing room reunites behind him in the United States, Mexico and Canada will shape Uruguay's ceiling far more than any tactical board.
[...]
The draw was unkind. In Group H, Uruguay share the section with world No. 1 and tournament favourite Spain, World Cup debutants Cape Verde, and Saudi Arabia. La Celeste open against Saudi Arabia on June 15 at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami, then face Cape Verde there on June 21, before a likely group-deciding clash with Spain on June 26 at the Estadio Akron in Guadalajara. The realistic target is second place behind Spain and a route through the round of 32; topping the group, as the brief frames it, would mean upsetting the team our model rates highest.
[...]
The squad still carries genuine quality. Real Madrid's Federico Valverde is among the best midfielders in the world, Darwin Núñez leads the line in the post-Suárez and Cavani era, and the defensive spine of captain José María Giménez and Barcelona's Ronald Araújo can frustrate anyone on their day. If Bielsa gets buy-in and the back line holds, a deep knockout run is not fantasy for a nation that has reached four World Cup semi-finals. But the path likely runs through one of Spain, Argentina or France early, and the margins are thin.
[...]
Honest verdict: Uruguay are outsiders, not contenders. Our model parks them deep in the longshot tier, far adrift of group rivals and clear favourites Spain. That reflects a talented but turbulent side capable of a quarter-final on a good run and an early exit on a bad one. This is the 12th time South Korea has participated in the World Cup, but the only time they’ve made it past the Round of 16 was on home soil in 2002. They are coming off a very impressive qualifying campaign and are, without a doubt, the second-best team in Asia behind Japan. They are in a very favorable group with Mexico, South Africa, and the Czech Republic, so could we see them make a deep run this summer?
[...]
South Korea was insanely impressive during World Cup qualifying. Not only did they go unbeaten, but they had a +18.03 expected goal differential in only 16 matches.
[...]
The worry for South Korea is they really haven’t played that difficult of competition. Myung-bo Hong took over as manager after the Asian Cup and has done a really nice job.

Like I have said many times, I don’t put too much stock into friendlies, but with a team like South Korea, which hasn’t played anyone close to the caliber they will at the World Cup, it becomes relevant.

Credit to the South Korean FA for scheduling many difficult opponents. They’ve had some mixed results, beating some lower-tier World Cup teams, but getting dominated by the likes of Brazil and the Ivory Coast.
